subtitle: When Voices Fade, Ink Must Speak

panels.shot: dramatic three-quarter view of a monk seated before blank palm leaves, shadowed elders behind, city of Vallabhi faint in the distance
panels.action: Devarddhigani Kshamashraman sits cross-legged before a low wooden desk stacked with blank palm-leaf strips, his gaze steady and grave, while robed Jain elders loom in the dim hall like fading memories.

dialogue.text: Centuries after Mahavira, as famine and forgetting thin the Jain voice, Devarddhigani at Vallabhi must ask: will the Agamas die as sound, or live as ink?

i18n.hi: महावीर के सदियों बाद, जब अकाल और भूल से जैन स्वर पतला पड़ता है, वल्लभी का देवर्द्धिगणि सोचता है: आगम ध्वनि बन कर मरें, या स्याही बन कर जिएँ?

panels.shot: wide aerial shot over western India, rivers and dry plains, dissolving into scattered monastic settlements
panels.action: A sweeping landscape of western India stretches under a hazy sky, small monasteries dotting the plains and hills, separated by rivers and distances that hint at isolation.

dialogue.text: After Mahavira’s nirvana, Jain monks carry his words from Magadha to Gujarat and beyond, relying on memory as they cross dry plains, shifting courts and fragile kingdoms.

i18n.hi: महावीर के निर्वाण के बाद जैन साधु मगध से गुजरात और आगे तक उसके वचन ढोते हैं, सूखे मैदान, बदलते दरबार, कमजोर राज्यों को याददाश्त के सहारे पार करते हुए।

panels.shot: interior of a simple ancient monastery, elders teaching young monks in oral recitation
panels.action: In a stone-pillared hall, an elder monk sits before a row of novices, eyes closed, palms up, chanting as the novices repeat in unison, the rhythm weaving through the still air.

dialogue.text: For generations, the Agamas are not books but breath: verses recited at dawn, patterns of sound guarded by lineages of teachers and students.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियों तक आगम किताब नहीं, सांस हैं: भोर में गाए गए पद, ध्वनि के रूप, जिन्हें गुरु‑शिष्य परंपराएँ पहरा देती हैं।

panels.shot: somber montage-style shot of drought-stricken land, abandoned monastery, and a lone monk on the road
panels.action: Dry, cracked earth spreads under a blazing sun, an abandoned monastery stands with doors open to dust, and a solitary monk walks a lonely road with a small bundle.

dialogue.text: Then famine, war and fear strike. Monasteries thin, lineages scatter, and with each elder lost, a portion of remembered scripture vanishes silently.

i18n.hi: फिर अकाल, युद्ध और डर वार करते हैं। मठ सूने पड़ते हैं, परंपराएँ बिखरती हैं, और हर वृद्ध के साथ कुछ शास्त्र चुपके से मिट जाता है।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Devarddhigani in middle age, listening intently to disputing monks in a modest hall
panels.action: Devarddhigani Kshamashraman, robed in white, sits calm yet attentive as two monks stand and argue, their gestures sharp, in a modest stone hall lit by slanting afternoon light.

dialogue.text: By tradition, in the age remembered around the fifth century, one monk, Devarddhigani Kshamashraman, hears a disturbing pattern: elders disagree on the very wording of Mahavira’s teachings.

i18n.hi: परंपरा में, पाँचवीं सदी के आस‑पास याद किए गए समय में, एक भिक्षु देवर्द्धिगणि क्षमाश्रमण एक डरावना सुर सुनता है: स्वयं महावीर के वचन पर बुज़ुर्गों में मतभेद हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Devarddhigani’s face, thoughtful and troubled
panels.action: Devarddhigani’s lined face fills the frame, brows slightly knit, eyes lowered in thought, as faint silhouettes of chanting monks blur behind him like echoes.

dialogue.text: Jinadasagani’s Nandisutra-churni, centuries later, will recall this unease: that parts of the canon are already lost, and what remains is held in fallible minds.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद जिनदासगणि की नंदीसूत्र‑चूर्णि इसी बेचैनी को याद करेगी: कि कुछ आगम तो खो चुके हैं, और जो बचा है, वह भी नाशवान मन में टिका है।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Vallabhi city with scholarly buildings and monasteries
panels.action: The bustling city of Vallabhi spreads along a river, with tiled roofs, market streets, and, rising among them, quiet monastic complexes and halls of learning.

dialogue.text: Later Jain tradition names Vallabhi in Saurashtra as the place of decision—a city already known for learning, where merchants, monks and teachers share narrow streets.

i18n.hi: बाद की जैन कथाओं में सौराष्ट्र की वल्लभी को निर्णायक स्थल कहा गया—विद्या की नगरी, जहाँ व्यापारी, साधु और आचार्य तंग गलियों में मिलते हैं।

panels.shot: interior council hall wide shot, many monks assembled in rows, Devarddhigani at the center
panels.action: In a spacious pillared hall, rows of Jain monks sit facing inward, white robes forming a sea of stillness, as Devarddhigani sits at the central axis, calm yet commanding.

dialogue.text: Council traditions say Devarddhigani calls learned monks together. In their silence lies a hard question: can spoken heritage survive another century of loss?

i18n.hi: परिषद की कथाएँ कहती हैं: देवर्द्धिगणि विद्वान साधुओं को बुलाते हैं। उनकी खामोशी में एक कठिन प्रश्न है: बोलकर चले आ रहे विरासत को क्या एक और सदी के क्षय से बचाया जा सकता है?

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Devarddhigani rising to speak to the assembly
panels.action: Devarddhigani rises from his seat, hands folded at his chest, as the assembly looks up; shafts of light cut through dust motes, giving the moment a suspended weight.

dialogue.speaker: devarddhigani_kshamashraman
dialogue.text: If memory fails, shall we let the Teacher’s word dissolve, or bind it in script?

i18n.hi: अगर स्मृति चूके, तो क्या हम शिक्षक के वचन को घुल जाने दें, या उसे लिपि में बाँध दें?

panels.shot: over-shoulder shot from behind Devarddhigani, showing monks reacting, some nodding, some hesitant
panels.action: From behind Devarddhigani, the seated monks are seen exchanging glances; a few nod gravely, others look uneasy, fingers tightening around their rosaries.

dialogue.text: Putting scripture into writing is no easy step. Oral custodians fear frozen words may replace living discipline, yet the gaps in recollection grow wider each year.

i18n.hi: शास्त्र को लिखवा देना आसान कदम नहीं। मौखिक रक्षक डरते हैं कि जमी हुई पंक्तियाँ कहीं जिंदा साधना को न निगल जाएँ, पर याद की दरारें हर साल चौड़ी होती जाती हैं।

panels.shot: table-level shot of palm leaves, ink pots, and scribes preparing, with Devarddhigani overseeing
panels.action: A long wooden table is lined with palm leaves and simple ink pots; scribes sit ready, styluses in hand, while Devarddhigani stands behind them, overseeing with steady focus.

dialogue.text: According to the Jinacaritra of the Kalpasutra and later works like Jinaprabha’s Sandehavisausadhi, the council chooses courage: the Agamas will be written down.

i18n.hi: कल्पसूत्र के जिनचरित्र और बाद के जिनप्रभ के सन्देहविसौसधि जैसे ग्रंथों में परिषद का निर्णय साहस बन कर दर्ज है: आगम लिखे जाएँगे।

panels.shot: close shot on a scribe’s hand writing on palm leaf, Devarddhigani’s shadow falling across the leaf
panels.action: A scribe’s hand carefully traces letters on a palm leaf, the lines dark and deliberate, as Devarddhigani’s shadow falls over the script, anchoring the act.

dialogue.text: For days and perhaps months, reciters speak and scribes inscribe. Sound becomes symbol, and the fragile stream of memory hardens into visible lines.

i18n.hi: दिनों, शायद महीनों तक पाठक बोलते हैं, लेखक लिखते हैं। ध्वनि चिह्न बनती है, और नाज़ुक याद की धारा दृश्यमान रेखाओं में जम जाती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Devarddhigani reviewing a manuscript with other elders
panels.action: Devarddhigani and two elder monks sit around a manuscript, leaning in as they compare versions, lips moving silently, fingers marking disputed passages.

dialogue.text: Yet even here, unity is not complete. Different recensions surface, and not every Jain tradition will later accept the same list or number of Agamas.

i18n.hi: फिर भी यहाँ भी एकरूपता नहीं। अलग‑अलग पाठ निकलते हैं, और बाद की हर जैन परंपरा एक‑सी आगम सूची या संख्या नहीं मानती।

panels.shot: reflective close-up of Devarddhigani closing his eyes in contemplation
panels.action: Devarddhigani sits alone, manuscript rolled beside him, eyes closed, hands resting on his knees, as faint city sounds filter into the quiet cell.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars like Dundas and Jaini will later question details of date and place, reading this council as central memory rather than court record.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान डुण्डस और जैनी बाद में तिथि और स्थल के ब्योरे पर सवाल उठाएँगे, इस परिषद को दरबार की रिपोर्ट नहीं, सामूहिक स्मृति की धुरी मानते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of Vallabhi’s scholarly quarter, with people carrying manuscripts between buildings
panels.action: In Vallabhi’s learned quarter, monks and lay scholars move between stone buildings carrying wrapped bundles of palm leaves, while young students watch with curiosity.

dialogue.text: Whatever its exact coordinates in time, the act itself reshapes Jain life. Vallabhi emerges as a center where written Jain learning takes firm root.

i18n.hi: समय के सही निशान चाहे जैसे हों, यह कर्म खुद जैन जीवन को मोड़ देता है। वल्लभी वह केंद्र बन उठता है जहाँ लिखित जैन विद्या जड़ पकड़ती है।

panels.shot: symbolic low-angle shot of stacked manuscripts in a dim store-room, Devarddhigani silhouetted at the doorway
panels.action: Stacks of neatly bound palm-leaf manuscripts rest on shelves in a dim storeroom; at the doorway, Devarddhigani stands in silhouette, watching in silent guardianship.

dialogue.text: From this point, Jain monks can point not only to elders but to texts. The canon is no longer only a river of recitation but also a library of leaves.

i18n.hi: अब से जैन साधु केवल बुज़ुर्गों नहीं, ग्रंथों की ओर भी इशारा कर सकते हैं। canon अब केवल पाठ की नदी नहीं, पत्तों की लाइब्रेरी भी है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style montage of later centuries: different Jain monks reading manuscripts
panels.action: A visual montage shows monks of different centuries and robes seated in varied halls, each reading from palm-leaf or paper manuscripts, their faces lit by lamps.

dialogue.text: Over centuries, councils, commentators and sects will argue over which texts truly carry Mahavira’s voice, yet they argue now with written evidence at hand.

i18n.hi: सदियों तक परिषदें, टीकाकार और संप्रदाय बहस करेंगे कि कौन‑से ग्रंथ सचमुच महावीर की आवाज ढोते हैं, पर अब बहस हाथ में रखे लिखित सबूत के साथ होगी।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a manuscript line, then soft focus on Devarddhigani’s serene face behind it
panels.action: A line of script on aged palm leaf fills the frame, then soft focus reveals Devarddhigani’s serene face beyond, as if the words and the monk share one plane.

dialogue.text: In the Jain telling, Devarddhigani does not invent doctrine; he preserves what remains, accepting that fixing living speech into script is itself a risky, necessary vow.

i18n.hi: जैन कथा में देवर्द्धिगणि सिद्धांत गढ़ता नहीं; जो बचा है उसे सँभालता है, मानते हुए कि जीवित वाणी को लिपि में बाँधना खुद एक जोखिम भरा, पर ज़रूरी व्रत है।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of a quiet library in Vallabhi at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, a quiet library hall in Vallabhi glows with fading light, rows of manuscripts resting in stillness, as the figure of a lone monk walks between them.

dialogue.text: His legacy lies in this choice: when memory alone could no longer bear the weight of a tradition, Devarddhigani dared to let ink share the burden.

i18n.hi: उसकी विरासत इसी चुनाव में है: जब सिर्फ़ स्मृति परंपरा का भार उठाने में थक गई, देवर्द्धिगणि ने स्याही को भी यह बोझ उठाने की हिम्मत दी।

title_i18n.en: Devarddhigani Saves the Agamas in Ink
title_i18n.hi: देवर्द्धिगणि: आगमों को स्याही में बचाने वाला

subtitle_i18n.en: When Voices Fade, Ink Must Speak
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब आवाजें थक जाएँ, स्याही बोलेगी
